parts.note: tennis has a kind of fault served twice in a row, and the same word names a two-horse bet that appeals to punters, read here as 'betters', people who bet

explanation.surface: Snobbish moralising: the vices that appeal to the upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Betters' looks like social superiors, but it means people who place bets. A double fault loses a tennis point; a double is a bet on two races.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tennis fault served twice over and a wager linking two selections.

clue.text: Told a chap he wasn't such a swine after all ?

definitions.text: Told a chap he wasn't such a swine after all ?

parts.words: Told a chap he wasn't such a swine after all
parts.note: reads the word as undoing an insult: calling someone a swine is abuse, and taking it back un-abuses him

explanation.surface: An apology to a man previously insulted.
explanation.walkthrough: The word really means freed from a false belief; split as dis-abused it suggests reversing abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct someone's mistaken belief; here read as cancelling earlier abuse.

clue.text: Kingdom appears to fall to eastern republic

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom
rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: A kingdom seems to come under an eastern republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears to' is a link phrase joining Kingdom to the pieces that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a republic in eastern Europe.

parts.note: not an intellectual but a tall man, one whose brow is high off the ground

explanation.surface: An intellectual sort of poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-brow' suggests intellectual, but here it is literal: a tall chap. Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was an American poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was the American poet of Hiawatha; split, his name suggests a tall man.

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters of the word fast fall over into a new order

parts.note: a ford is a shallow place for crossing a river

explanation.surface: A quick journey that passes through a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like the journey, but it signals rearranging FAST into STAF. STAFFORD is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is an English county town.

clue.text: Roughly two hundred wild trees in Northants

indicators.note: roughly means the letters of two are treated loosely and rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: wild means the letters of trees run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Around two hundred trees growing wild in a Midlands county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' turns TWO into TOW and 'wild' turns TREES into ESTER, either side of C. Northants is Northamptonshire, an English Midlands county; Towcester is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Towcester is a market town in Northamptonshire.

definitions.meaning: a point where a road or river divides in two
the pronged utensil that carries food to the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a dividing point in a road or tree and the eating utensil that lifts food.

parts.note: O, the figure nought, stands for no
a rating is a set of marks given in assessment

explanation.surface: An exam that gives no marks for oral work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Orating means making a speech, formal speaking.

definitions.meaning: the sweet fruit of a palm tree
a calendar month gives about thirty days, each a calendar day

explanation.definitionFit: It means both a palm fruit and calendar days, which each month provides.

indicators.note: parts means a piece of the words lake pilot is taken out

explanation.surface: A lake pilot hands over his cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts with' suggests giving up, but 'parts' signals the run inside lake pilot. A kepi is a French military cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a flat-topped peaked military cap.

parts.note: not an athlete heaving a metal ball but the medical instrument that puts in a shot, an injection

explanation.surface: An athlete who throws the shot.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shot' is also an injection, and this is the device that gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical needle-and-plunger device delivers an injection, colloquially a shot.

parts.note: war, used as an adjective as in 'war talk', is the bellicose sort
a rant is loud, overblown talk

explanation.surface: Defending warmongering speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the reading 'war rant' as one example of bellicose bombast.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant an action is to give grounds for it, to justify it.

clue.text: If beer's roughly about £4, that's Aubrey's work

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes around the money piece
roughly means the letters of if beer's are handled loosely and rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound (librum) and IV is the Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: Grumbling over the price of beer, with a nod to a seventeenth-century author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges IFBEERS into BRIEFES, and 'about' puts L IV (pounds four) inside it. The OCR dropped the pound sign. John Aubrey wrote the gossipy biographies called Brief Lives.
explanation.definitionFit: John Aubrey's best-known book is a collection of short biographies with this title.

definitions.meaning: to fail to catch or hit something
the title used in addressing an unmarried woman

explanation.definitionFit: To not catch a train is one sense; the other is the form of address for an unmarried woman.

clue.text: Love to take in unusually dim people in government !

indicators.note: to take in means the love letter is taken inside the anagram
unusually means the letters of dim are set out of their usual order

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, written O
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Romantic ambitions to recruit stupid people into government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges DIM into DMI, and 'to take in' puts O inside it, making DOMI before NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Domination is rule or control, the exercise of governing power.

clue.text: Poet is reserved about foreign female

indicators.note: about means the shy word wraps around the female

parts.note: a reserved person is shy
elle is French for 'she'

explanation.surface: A bashful poet keeps his distance from a woman from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ELLE inside SHY. Percy Bysshe Shelley was a Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley was an English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Time was when the old-fashioned strayed all over the place

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the definite article

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Nostalgia for the days when traditional folk wandered everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old-fashioned' gives YE, as in 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe', and 'all over the place' rearranges YE and STRAYED together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both refer to the past: 'time was when' means in former days.

definitions.meaning: considered means reflected on, as in 'I gave it some'... past tense of think
the idiom 'quick as ...' makes the word a byword for speed

explanation.definitionFit: It is the past tense of think, meaning considered, and the proverbial measure of speed in 'swift as thought'.

clue.text: Perhaps Hamlet appears to Tree ill-constructed

indicators.note: ill-constructed means the letters of to, Tree and ill are badly built and reordered

explanation.surface: Hamlet seemed badly built to the actor Herbert Beerbohm Tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' is both fodder and the start of 'ill-constructed', where 'constructed' signals the rearrangement. Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager who played Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is the name part in the play, an example of the lead part named in the title.

clue.text: Fruit supplied by Moss and Cook

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so the letters of moss and are reworked

explanation.surface: Fruit provided by a pair of tradesmen, Moss and Cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moss and Cook' reads like a firm's name, but 'Cook' rearranges MOSSAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsons are small purple plums.

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of mine is M

indicators.note: backs means the girl's name is read from the back

parts.note: Stella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from Minehead, a Somerset seaside resort, supports the strikers.
explanation.walkthrough: Minehead is a resort in Somerset; here it means the head of 'mine'. 'backs' turns STELLA into ALLETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallets are hammers, tools used for striking.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the torn word goes around the intention

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, meaning torn
an aim is an intention

explanation.surface: Clothes ripped by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: RENT goes around AIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing.

parts.note: not a prophet but a malicious look: the seer is the organ that sees, and it brings bad luck

explanation.surface: A fortune teller best kept away from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seer' looks like a prophet but is literally something that sees, here a malevolent gaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A malevolent look believed to cast harm is the thing that sees and should be shunned.

parts.note: not a protest against motoring but the thing a golfer strikes off the tee

explanation.surface: Someone protesting against having to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb of protest, but it is a noun: the thing struck in a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf or cricket a drive is a stroke that sends the sphere in play a long way.

definitions.meaning: an old poetic word for a sword
Ibsen's verse drama about a stern priest

explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic word for a blade and the title of Ibsen's 1865 drama.

clue.text: Write me something in case we get thoughtful!

indicators.note: in means the something word is placed inside the case

parts.note: the dative is a grammatical case
it can stand for an unnamed something

explanation.surface: A request to write a letter in a time of reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Write me' tells you to put down ME first; 'in' puts IT inside DATIVE, the grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone meditative is lost in contemplation, i.e. pensive.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MPS was Member of the Pharmaceutical Society, a qualified man dispensing medicines

explanation.surface: A man handing out evil spirits, or bad liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man dispensing' gives MPS, the letters once after a British pharmacist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Imps are small mischievous demons.

parts.note: not the end of the pitch the bowler runs from, but the end of a cricket batting order, where the weak-batting bowlers come in

explanation.surface: The end of the cricket pitch from which bowling is done.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the bowlers bat last, so they make up the end of the batting order.
explanation.definitionFit: The last batsmen in a cricket team, usually its bowlers, are called by this name for the rear.

parts.note: the famous medieval lover's name begins with, and so gives away, the name of the second son of Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: A lover betrays someone from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Abelard was the twelfth-century lover of Heloise; his name starts with ABEL, the brother killed by Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: Abelard is famous as the lover of Heloise in the twelfth century.

clue.text: Old card game of best quality — or reverse

parts.note: prime means of the best quality

indicators.note: reverse tells you to turn the little word or backwards

explanation.surface: An old card game: either top grade or the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' turns OR into RO after PRIME. Primero was a Tudor gambling card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Primero was a sixteenth-century gambling card game.

clue.text: Shows performance in a Norfolk town

indicators.note: in means the performance is placed inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, an English county
a play is a theatrical performance

explanation.surface: A show staged in a small East Anglian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PLAY inside DISS, a market town in Norfolk, the county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to exhibit it; exhibitions are such things.

parts.note: expire in its literal sense of breathe out: a sudden blast of air caused by a chill

explanation.surface: Someone dying abruptly of exposure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expire' looks like dying, but literally it means to breathe out.
explanation.definitionFit: An involuntary explosive exhalation through the nose, typical of having a chill.
